gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Futuristic and angular, Megrim draws every curve as thin as its straight stems. Noto Sans Oriya sits below with generous gaps in its curves and small letters nearly as tall as its capitals, so a shrunken heading would quickly lose out to it.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-osage: Hairline angles, then big soft bowls. Megrim is at its best being sharp and showy, while Noto Sans Osage is at its best filling the line with inflated, sweeping sans curves that stay open.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Megrim keeps its joins as thick as its stems, giving a stencil-like, angular look. Noto Sans Osmanya follows in plain sans, its oversized lowercase and wide, easy s turns making the strongest contrast.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hmong: Contemporary in feel, Megrim looks drawn with a marker tip, every stroke held to one measured thickness. Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong answers in plain sans, with a high x-height and rounds that gap like a cracked bangle, which is the strongest part of the pairing.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-palmyrene: Angular crossbars as thick as the stems, set above a body of curves that stop short instead of closing. Noto Sans Palmyrene would read lightly and briskly across a long page.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-pau-cin-hau: Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau reads clean and modern, its open-ended curves leaving room to breathe and its capitals barely above the lowercase. Megrim above it has no thick-and-thin shifts at all, so the sharp angular heading and the softer sans-serif text sit together without crowding.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Noto Sans PhagsPa reads approachably, with c openings you can see through and capitals rising only gently above the small letters. Megrim's steady pen pressure from first letter to last is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-phoenician: Sharp, futuristic caps built from lines of one constant thickness. Noto Sans Phoenician then reads easily over a long page, its generous lowercase and wide-ended s curves keeping the sans-serif text open.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-psalter-pahlavi: Megrim's stencil-cut feel, with every stroke at a single weight, gives the heading an angular, futuristic edge. Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi's plain sans gaping e and low capitals are the pair's strongest quality.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Professional in tone, Megrim holds an unvarying line thickness through every sharp, angular letter. Yet Noto Sans Rejang, with lowercase counters like wide glass portholes, would read through a long page with clear sans-serif gaps in each c, e, s and a.
